listings.mrt_info: 1 min (120 m) from CC14 Lorong Chuan MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: A spacious 1,475 sqft 99LH 3BR at $1,322 psf, ~17% below the district median PSF of $1,594, with a 500-unit base and an MRT literally at the doorstep (120m to Lorong Chuan). Strong resale CAGR (6.4%/yr, 69 txns), deep liquidity and a sub-$2M entry make this a credible value play despite the 1995 vintage.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Entry PSF $1,322 vs URA median $1,594 is a genuine ~17% discount on a large-format unit, and the 6.4%/yr resale-only appreciation over 69 transactions is well above the OCR baseline. 120m to Lorong Chuan MRT and Serangoon NEX nearby anchor both rental and resale demand; 500 units gives a deep buyer pool. Real en-bloc optionality (377,682 sqft land, second-largest in the cluster) is a tail upside, though the estate just spent on upgrading so it is not imminent. Knocked off Strong Buy by 31-year age (remaining lease ~68yr, financing/maintenance headwinds building) and reported pest/security gripes.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Deep tenant pool from Lorong Chuan/Serangoon transit access and proximity to schools; large layout appeals to families. Yield is modest (older-estate rents lag new launches) but occupancy should be reliable.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 6.4%/yr resale-only CAGR over 69 txns is robust and above OCR baseline; the PSF gap to district median gives room to converge upward. Age caps the ceiling, so expect steady rather than explosive appreciation.

listings.mrt_info: 9 min (750 m) from CP1 Pasir Ris MRT Station

Strong 6.9%/yr resale CAGR over a thick 206-transaction base, with Pasir Ris's CRL + DTL extension and the Pasir Ris Central redevelopment as forward catalysts.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: This is the most data-backed entry in the batch: 206 URA resale transactions giving a high-confidence 6.9%/yr CAGR, on a modern (2016) well-maintained 892-unit development at a $1,440 psf discount to the $1,561 median. Build quality and management reviews are positive after ~8 years. Sub-mid-$2M for a 1,389 sqft 3BR keeps it in the deep buyer band. Held below Strong Buy by the 750m (9-min) MRT walk — fine but not doorstep — and by OCR-far-east location capping the appreciation ceiling versus RCR peers.

listings.mrt_info: 10 min (820 m) from DT30 Bedok Reservoir MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: A very large 1,539 sqft 99LH 3BR at $1,222 psf, ~10% under the $1,352 district median, in a 720-unit Bedok Reservoir development backing onto the reservoir. URA resale CAGR is a strong 7.3%/yr over 129 txns, but the 2000-vintage estate carries real management, leak and noise complaints that temper the value case.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: The numbers are attractive — $1,222 psf vs $1,352 median, 7.3%/yr resale CAGR over 129 txns, a huge 1,539 sqft layout under $1.9M, and reservoir-fronting amenity. But qualitative findings are a genuine drag: residents report poor MCST management, recurring unit leaks (especially upper units), evening noise, and it being the oldest/most run-down condo in the Bedok Reservoir cluster. With Bedok Reservoir MRT a 10-min/820m walk and 26-year lease decay (~74yr remaining), the appreciation may already reflect a low base catching up rather than durable quality. Mixed signals net to Neutral.

listings.mrt_info: 1 min (100 m) from CR11 Ang Mo Kio MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: A 2014, high-finish 34-storey landmark beside AMK Hub with the upcoming CR11 Cross Island Line interchange essentially at the doorstep (100m). The listed $1,497 psf sits far below the $2,040 district median, but that gap is misleading — Centro is a SOHO/loft-stack development, so the headline median is skewed by smaller premium units; still, an integrated-transit 3BR at this price with CRL incoming is a strong setup.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: The standout catalyst is CR11 Ang Mo Kio becoming a Cross Island Line interchange (~2030) at 100m — within-500m future MRT is the strongest single uplift in the rubric, and 100m is doorstep. Pair that with AMK Hub integration, a well-finished 2014 building (DP Architects, one of AMK's tallest, premium finishes) and a 6.2%/yr resale CAGR over 77 txns. The $1,497-vs-$2,040 psf gap overstates cheapness (loft/SOHO unit mix skews the district median), so I treat value as fair-to-slightly-positive rather than a deep discount. Limited common-area space and a more couple/expat-than-family layout temper broad upgrader appeal, holding it to Buy.

Reviews note limited common-area/facility space; layout suits couples/expats more than large families

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 6.2%/yr resale CAGR over 77 txns is solid; the CRL interchange at 100m is a concrete, high-impact catalyst that should drive above-baseline appreciation into 2030. Value is fair once the unit-mix-skewed median is corrected.

listings.mrt_info: 3 min (260 m) from CC12 Bartley MRT Station

Strong location and liquidity, but the development carries documented finish/defect complaints and an unresponsive defects-management reputation.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: D13/Bartley is a structurally strong RCR-adjacent node: 260m to Bartley CCL station, central connectivity, reputable schools nearby. The 250-txn URA base gives high-confidence 6.2%/yr appreciation, and $1,709 psf is a real ~16% discount to the $2,024 median on a modern 2016 unit. The cap to Buy (not Strong Buy) is the well-documented build-quality history — visible wall defects, marble scratches, noisy WCs, poor appliance/defect-handling — which is a real resale and own-experience risk to verify unit-by-unit; choose a well-maintained stack.

listings.mrt_info: 11 min (950 m) from EW4 Tanah Merah MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: A low-quantum (under $1.39M) 1,173 sqft 99LH 3BR in a quiet 288-unit Tanah Merah hilltop enclave, at $1,181 psf roughly in line with the $1,205 district median. Strong 7.1%/yr resale CAGR, but a small boutique base, an 11-min/950m MRT walk and reports of weak maintenance temper the case.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: The low $1.385M quantum is the real draw — broadest possible buyer pool and lowest absolute risk in the batch — and the 7.1%/yr resale CAGR is strong. But fundamentals are mixed: only 288 units (thinner liquidity, 68 txns), a long 11-min/950m walk to Tanah Merah MRT, and reviews flagging poor maintenance and a development that looks older than its 2004 age, plus a small pool for resident count. PSF is essentially at median ($1,181 vs $1,205), so there is no real value discount cushioning those weaknesses. Quiet hilltop exclusivity is a livability plus but not an investment catalyst. Nets to Neutral.

listings.mrt_info: 8 min (630 m) from CC12 Bartley MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: A brand-new (2026 TOP) compact 1,044 sqft 3BR from boutique 115-unit Bartley Vue at a steep $2,395 psf and $2.5M quantum. The system already flagged new-launch bias and discounted the headline rate to 4.07%/yr; at this price/PSF on a tiny development with a high quantum, the risk/reward is poor.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Three things stack against this as an investment: (1) $2,395 psf is above the $2,346 district median and you are buying at peak new-launch pricing — the bias-adjusted appreciation is only 4.07%/yr (vs 6.47% resale-only), so the system is explicitly warning the headline CAGR re-introduces developer inflation; (2) $2.5M for a compact 1,044 sqft 3BR pushes past the deep-buyer sweet spot into a thinner pool, with little built-in upside; (3) only 115 units = boutique, illiquid, minimal facilities, and the MRT is a 630m/8-min walk with Circle-Line-only access. Buying a just-TOP unit at developer-peak PSF in D19 with no discount and a high quantum is the classic overpay-at-launch trap. Avoid for a 5-7yr investment hold.

River-view stacks are the only ones I'd consider; the rest are ordinary aging OCR stock. The above-median pricing on a no-MRT, dated estate caps this at Neutral.
